title: GETTING YOUR RIGHTS BACK!: A Fresh Start After A Felony
description: GETTING YOUR RIGHTS BACK A Fresh Start After a Felony Georgia Edition YOUR PAST DOES NOT HAVE TO DEFINE YOUR FUTURE. A felony conviction can create challenges that affect your rights, opportunities, employment, and future. But your past does not have to determine where your story ends. Getting Your Rights Back: A Fresh Start After a Felony is a practical, easy-to-understand guide designed to help individuals in Georgia learn about their rights, understand available restoration options, and take informed steps toward a fresh start. WHAT YOU WILL LEARN: Voting Rights: Understand when voting rights are restored and what steps may be necessary to register. Civil and Political Rights: Explore the process of applying to restore certain civil and political rights. Georgia Pardons: Learn what a pardon means, general eligibility requirements, and what it does and does not accomplish. Firearm Rights: Understand why firearm-rights restoration is a separate legal process. Criminal Record Restriction: Learn about Georgia's record restriction process and how eligibility may affect your options. Employment and Background Checks: Explore ways to address criminal-history concerns when pursuing employment opportunities. Applications and Documentation: Understand the importance of records, paperwork, eligibility, and application procedures. Your Fresh Start: Discover practical steps for moving forward and rebuilding your future. You do not have to figure everything out at once. This guide helps break down complicated topics into manageable information so you can better understand your options and know where to seek additional help. title: Burnout Broke My Body: A Capacity-Based System to Catch Burnout Before Your Body Does
description: Your calendar looks survivable. Something underneath it isn't. You're the one people count on, at work and at home. From the outside it looks handled. But your focus, your sleep, and your body keep wearing down. Often the body notices first. Capacity is what you actually have. Load is what you're carrying. When Load exceeds Capacity, that's Bad Math . Right-Sizing changes the plan until it fits. Maria Vought, a nurse turned operations leader, ran capacity math for a living until her own ran out. Her story opens the book. The rest is a system you can use the same week: small changes, no wellness lectures, and no giving up your ambitions. Inside: The Daily Capacity Snapshot: a two-minute check on whether today fits The STOP Check: four questions that turn a quick yes into a better one The Pressure Map and Access Map: find what's driving the strain, and decide what gets access to you The Reduced-Capacity Plan: built on a better day, before you need it If this sounds like someone you love, it was written for them too. And it's for anyone who keeps saying "after this season." You are not the problem. title: GET THE ORDER RIGHT: Why Smart, Hardworking People Stay Broke and the Four Steps That Fina
description: You work hard. You earn a decent income. You do most things sensibly. So why won’t the numbers move? Most people try to fix their money with tactics: a better budget, a hot tip, one more side hustle. But the problem usually isn’t effort or intelligence. It’s sequence. Smart, hardworking people stay broke because they do the right things in the wrong order: investing before they’re stable, chasing growth before they’ve built strength, multiplying risk before they’ve earned the right to take it. GET THE ORDER RIGHT sets out the four steps that build wealth, and the order that makes them work: 1. Stabilize. Stop the leaks and build a floor that holds when life gets expensive. 2. Strengthen. Turn that floor into resilience: protection, margin and habits that survive a bad year. 3. Grow. Put money to work steadily, on purpose, and on a timeline you control. 4. Multiply. Only now let compounding, leverage and bigger bets do the heavy lifting. Inside, you’ll learn: Why the same financial move can build wealth at one step and quietly destroy it at another How to tell which step you’re really on, not the one you’d like to be on The hidden patterns in how you see, frame and react to money that keep you circling the same place How to read the feedback your finances give you, and change the pattern instead of just trying harder How to make decisions that hold up over decades, not just the next good year This is not a book about budgeting harder or finding the perfect investment. It’s a practical framework for building wealth in the right sequence, so that each step supports the next instead of collapsing under it. title: Grace Broke Right On Time (Special Edition)
An American Problem: How the Country Built--and the Supreme Court Broke--the Voting Rights
description: The rise and fall of the Voting Rights Act, from the triumph of its passage in 1965 to its evisceration by the Supreme Court in their 2013 decision in Shelby County v. Holder The Voting Rights Act of 1965 finally made good on the promise of the Fifteenth Amendment, which nearly a century before had granted Black Americans the right to vote. The Voting Rights Act was the crowning achievement of the Civil Rights Movement, which had battled for years against voting laws that made it all but impossible for Black Americans to cast a ballot. The act was a resounding success, bringing Americans of all races and ethnicities into the democratic process. And then, in 2013, the Supreme Court brought this progress to a screeching halt with their decision in Shelby County v. Holder . In this book, Michael Miller and Kevin Morris offer a sweeping history of the Voting Rights Act and the attacks it has suffered. Miller and Morris explain that central to the act's success was its requirement that states and localities with a history of discrimination get federal permission to change their voting rules—a novel approach known as "preclearance." It was this requirement that the Shelby County decision eviscerated. Miller and Morris trace the devastating effect of Shelby County , using advanced research techniques to prove that the decision unleashed racially discriminatory voting policies. The result is a nation in which Americans of color cast fewer ballots, and in which the ballots they do cast count for less. But the story does not end there: the Supreme Court continues to undermine what remains of the Voting Rights Act. What President Lyndon B. Johnson called "an American problem," formerly kept in check by a strong federal law, once again threatens voting rights.  ©2026 Princeton Univ

title: Broke (Broken Deeds MC Book 2)
description: Broke must be rough, dominant, and confident. Stepping into his new role as MC Vice President, the mask he wears screams "Don't screw with me!" but that just hides the part he can't show. Inside this sweet, shy man are insecurities stemming from trauma he encountered as a teenager that still haunt him. Roan is as sweet as they come. The epitome of pure; good, honest and innocent. Thrown into danger by her job, she's attacked by a member of the Russian mob. Left lying helpless in the hospital, one phone call binds her to the rough, handsome biker who would do anything to protect her. With danger lurking she has no other option but to hide beneath his wings. Both hide behind themselves, yet are determined to force the other to become the person they truly are. Will they each overcome their inner battles as well as the threat from the Russian mob who leaves a trail of bodies in its wake? Will Broke be able to save Roan's life or let his own slip through his fingers? Each book in the Broken Deeds MC series is a complete standalone story featuring a new couple.
